reproduction_target: GeneJEPA, a self-supervised Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture foundation model for scRNA-seq: (a) Tahoe-100M streaming ingest + log1p / global Z-score preprocessing, (b) Perceiver-encoder JEPA pretraining with EMA teacher and VICReg collapse prevention on 4x NVIDIA H100 under PyTorch Lightning DDP, and (c) a set of frozen-encoder downstream evaluations - PBMC3k and Human Lung Cell Atlas cell-identity probes (logistic regression, cosine kNN, k-means, UMAP), sci-Plex v3 dose-response ridge regression, the NeurIPS Open Problems perturbation-prediction benchmark probe (Morgan fingerprints + multi-output ridge), multi-read test-time scaling, and a zero-shot in-silico TP53 knockout in latent space. No wet-lab component; the entire paper is a computational-reproduction target.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-analysis extracted from sections 3 (Large-Scale Implementation Details: Dataset and Preprocessing / Efficient Data Loading / Training Configuration), 4.1-4.4 (Results with embedded protocol prose), and Appendix A (Hyperparameter Details). The paper has no separate 'Methods' block: protocol text is distributed through the Results narrative, and the hyperparameter tables (Model Configuration, Training Configuration, Data and Experiment Configuration) are supplied as figure graphics rather than machine-readable text. Architecture description subsections (Tokenization, Perceiver Encoder, Cross-attention, Latent processing, Global readout, Masking Strategy and Predictor, Teacher Network, Loss Formulation, Predictive Loss, VICReg) are model-definition prose, folded into the C2 pretraining step rather than counted as separate invocations. Baseline-backbone embedding (scGPT, UCE) is one step. The public repository https://github.com/BiostateAI/GeneJEPA contains ONLY the pretraining package (genejepa/models.py, tokenizer.py, data.py, train.py, configs.py); it contains no evaluation, benchmark, probe, figure, or knockout code, so every downstream-evaluation step (C3-C9) has code=0 at prose level.

steps.label: Tahoe-100M ingest and preprocessing: Hugging Face datasets streaming from disk via a custom PyTorch Lightning DataModule with DDP-safe file sharding; log(1+x) transform then standardization by global mean/SD 'precomputed from a large subset of the training data'; large shuffle buffer for train, shuffling disabled for validation

GeneJEPA pretraining: Perceiver encoder over unordered gene sets with gene-identity + Fourier expression tokenizer, EMA teacher, masked-target predictive loss with VICReg variance-covariance regularization; AdamW (weight decay 2e-4, 1-D params and embedding tables excluded), cosine LR schedule with linear warmup, bfloat16 mixed precision, 4x NVIDIA H100 80GB, DDP with find_unused_parameters=True; full hyperparameters in Appendix A tables

PBMC3k cell-identity evaluation: embed ~3k cells with frozen encoders, create labels once by clustering and mapping clusters to canonical immune types with marker genes, fit UMAP on test embeddings only, then train a logistic-regression probe and a cosine kNN reader on the train split and report Macro F1 / Accuracy on the held-out split

Human Lung Cell Atlas evaluation: embed all cells with the frozen encoder; multiclass logistic regression with L2 regularization, split stratified by cell type 80/10/10, hyperparameters selected by five-fold CV on the training set; k-means on test embeddings with k = number of annotated types; UMAP fit on test embeddings only; Macro F1, accuracy, confusion matrix, per-class F1 vs class support (Spearman rho = 0.85)

sci-Plex v3 drug dose-response regression: pseudobulk aggregation of cells by context keys (cell line, compound, time), random 80/20 train/test partition shared across models, RidgeCV over a log-spaced alpha grid with five-fold CV on the training set only; metrics RMSE, MAE, MedAE, NRMSE-IQR, rRMSE vs global-median baseline, median per-context MAE + IQR, absolute mean bias

Baseline foundation-model embeddings: scGPT (Cui et al., 2024) and Universal Cell Embeddings / UCE (Rosen et al., 2023) used as frozen feature extractors with no fine-tuning; ridge readout alpha tuned on the same log-spaced grid by five-fold CV with an identical protocol across backbones

NeurIPS Open Problems perturbation-prediction benchmark probe: official file contracts and metrics, AnnData train/test matrices with a differential-expression layer, directional significance score S clipped to [-4, 4], gene order fixed by var_names and test row order by the provided id_map, 255 test profiles x 18,211 genes; per cell type a pseudo-expression vector formed by averaging the positive part of log fold change, Morgan fingerprint radius 2 / 2,048 bits per compound, concatenated with log dose (micromolar); multi-output ridge with the ridge parameter selected on a compound- and cell-type-grouped held-out split, followed by per-gene affine calibration and clipping; five official row-wise metrics (cosine, Pearson, Spearman, MAE, RMSE)

Multi-read test-time scaling: repeat the read over more genes while keeping latent computation fixed and aggregate the resulting embeddings, reported as directionality-metric improvement on the NeurIPS benchmark relative to the single-pass probe

Zero-shot in-silico TP53 knockout: build a per-gene perturbation vector from the frozen encoder by contrasting a wild-type-like set S_WT(g) and a mutant-like set S_MUT(g) drawn from Tahoe-100M using cell-line metadata when available, 'otherwise a conservative proxy (quantiles of log-expression or pathway activity, stratified within cell line)'; apply the direction to a new wild-type cell embedding and read out biological consequences in latent space without decoding to counts

headline.static_readiness: 0/9 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 2/9 steps (C1 Tahoe-100M ingest/preprocessing, C2 GeneJEPA pretraining) reach the stage-1 ceiling RI: the pretraining package is public at https://github.com/BiostateAI/GeneJEPA, the training corpus is CC0 on Hugging Face, the hyperparameters are tabulated in Appendix A, and a uv.lock lockfile plus a documented 'uv sync' install path constitute an environment-lock CLAIM (unverified at stage 1, so version stays at 1). The remaining 7 steps cap at NI because the repository ships only the pretraining package (models/tokenizer/data/train/configs) and contains no evaluation, benchmark, probe, figure, or knockout code; every downstream result (PBMC3k, HLCA, sci-Plex, Open Problems, test-time scaling, TP53 knockout) would have to be reimplemented from narrative prose. Stage-2 code verification could lift C1/C2 toward R-star; it cannot lift C3-C9 because there is no artifact to read.
headline.coverage: 9 computational steps assessed from Results/Implementation prose and Appendix A; 0 wet-lab steps (pure-computational paper). No dedicated Methods or Code-availability section exists; a 'Data availability and licensing' section is present, and the code/weights links appear only in the author-note header (Code: GitHub repository; Weights: Hugging Face).

gaps.where: All seven downstream-evaluation steps (C3 PBMC3k, C4 HLCA, C5 sci-Plex, C6 baseline backbones, C7 Open Problems probe, C8 test-time scaling, C9 TP53 knockout)
gaps.missing: The public repository contains only the pretraining package (genejepa/models.py, tokenizer.py, data.py, train.py, configs.py, pyproject.toml, uv.lock). No evaluation scripts, benchmark harness, probe-fitting code, figure-generation code, or in-silico-knockout code is released, so all reported results except the pretraining run itself are prose-only.
gaps.how_to_close: Add an eval/ or benchmarks/ subpackage (or a companion repo) with the embedding-extraction, probe-fitting, benchmark-submission, test-time-scaling, and knockout-vector scripts, plus the exact commands and configs used to produce Figures 2-6.

gaps.where: Software environment for the whole pipeline
gaps.missing: No container image or digest is provided, and the paper text pins nothing: the README states only floor constraints ('Python >= 3.11, PyTorch >= 2.6'). A uv.lock is present in the repository, but at stage 1 this is an unverified CLAIM: it is not referenced from the paper, no commit SHA or release tag is cited (the repository has zero tags/releases), CUDA/driver and hardware assumptions (4x H100, bfloat16) are outside any lock, and the lock covers the pretraining package only, not the absent evaluation code.
gaps.how_to_close: Cut a tagged release / archive to Zenodo and cite the exact commit or DOI in the paper; publish a container digest covering the CUDA stack; extend the lock to cover the evaluation dependencies (RDKit or equivalent for Morgan fingerprints, scanpy/umap-learn, scGPT and UCE).

gaps.where: C1 global normalization statistics; C4 HLCA snapshot; C5 sci-Plex preprocessing; C7 benchmark data
gaps.missing: The global mean/SD used for Z-score normalization are 'precomputed from a large subset of the training data' with the subset undefined, and the resulting global_stats.json / foundation_gene_map.parquet are not deposited (the README shows only how to regenerate them). The HLCA download is cited only as 'via the Human Cell Atlas Data Portal' with no version/snapshot or cell count. sci-Plex preprocessing is deferred to 'the standard preprocessing used across our benchmarks', which is never defined. The Open Problems benchmark release/version and the PBMC3k source file are not pinned.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the derived normalization statistics and gene map as fixed artifacts; cite exact dataset snapshot identifiers/versions (HLCA release, Open Problems benchmark version, PBMC3k file URL and checksum) and write down the shared preprocessing recipe explicitly.

gaps.where: C3, C4, C5, C8, C9 protocol parameters
gaps.missing: Random seeds are not stated anywhere despite randomized splits (PBMC3k, sci-Plex 80/20, HLCA 80/10/10), UMAP fits, k-means initialization, and a large shuffle buffer. The PBMC3k clustering algorithm, resolution, and marker-gene list used to create labels are unstated. UMAP hyperparameters (n_neighbors, min_dist, metric) are unstated. The C8 multi-read aggregation rule and the number of reads are not specified. In C9 the mutant-like/wild-type-like set definition falls back to an explicitly disjunctive proxy ('quantiles of log-expression OR pathway activity') with no thresholds, quantile cutoffs, or set sizes.
gaps.how_to_close: Report seeds, the clustering/marker protocol, UMAP and k-means settings, the multi-read count and aggregation function, and a single determinate rule (with thresholds and set sizes) for constructing the knockout direction.

gaps.where: C6 baseline backbones scGPT and UCE
gaps.missing: Baselines are invoked by citation only: no version, no repository URL, no checkpoint identifier, and no gene-vocabulary/input-preparation detail for either scGPT or UCE, even though 'identical inputs (same counts matrix, gene budget, and split)' is asserted.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact scGPT and UCE releases and checkpoint files, and release the adapter code that maps the shared counts matrix into each baseline's expected input format.

gaps.where: Appendix A hyperparameter tables (Model Configuration, Training Configuration, Data and Experiment Configuration)
gaps.missing: The three hyperparameter tables are embedded as figure graphics in the JATS record rather than as machine-readable table markup, so the pretraining configuration cannot be extracted programmatically from the paper; it must be cross-read against genejepa/configs.py.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the hyperparameter tables as text tables and/or ship the exact config file used for the reported run in the repository.
